newsitem.title: USA: Systems says unable to meet obligations. [CORRECTED 22:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Systems says unable to meet obligations. [CORRECTED 22:15 GMT]

text.p: Systems Communications Inc said Wednesday that it is experiencing cash flow difficulties due to continuing operating losses and is not able to meet all of its short-term or long-term obligations as they become due.
The company said it is reorganizing its corporate structure due to these cash flow difficulties and is attempting to raise additional capital in order to fund ongoing operations.
The company said it has filed neither its annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 1996 nor its quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 1997.

The company said it needs time to obtain an independent appraisal of the carrying amount of its investment in National Solutions Corp and make a determination of the recoverability of that investment and any impairment loss required to be recognized in the 1996 financial statements.

For the year ended December 31, 1996, the company said it had a loss of $5,450,000 compared with $5,808,000 for the previous year, before adjustments, if any, arising from management's review of the realization of the investment.

The loss per share for the year 1996 was $0.65 before possible adjustments, compared to a loss of $1.81 in 1995 on average shares outstanding of 8,349,459 and 3,201,991, respectively. (Corrects to clarify that company experienced a loss in fiscal 1995.)
Net revenues for 1996 were $5,009,981 compared with $2,984,884 in 1995, the company said.
The company said it repositioned itself as a healthcare management and information services business.
